question: In the second phase of art. 68, can an atenuante bring the provisional penalty below the minimum cominated for the offence?
quote: Art. 65 - São circunstâncias que sempre atenuam a pena:

readings.description: The second-phase result is floored at the cominated minimum: atenuantes reduce towards it but not past it (and, symmetrically, agravantes stop at the maximum).

citations.cite: STF, RE 597.270 QO-RG/RS (cited in TJDFT acórdão nº 695850; STF text not retrieved)

readings.description: 'Sempre atenuam' means always: an atenuante may reduce the penalty below the cominated minimum, which binds only the pena-base of the first phase.

question: May the same prior conviction be weighed as 'antecedentes' in the pena-base (art. 59) and again as the reincidência agravante (art. 61, I)?
quote: Art. 61 - São circunstâncias que sempre agravam a pena, quando não constituem ou qualificam o crime:

readings.description: No: a conviction that makes the agent reincidente is weighed only in the second phase; it cannot also raise the pena-base.
Yes: art. 59 and art. 61 are independent and each may take the same conviction into account.

question: What may count as (maus) 'antecedentes' under art. 59: pending inquiries or prosecutions? convictions older than art. 64, I's five-year window?
quote: Art. 59 - O juiz, atendendo à culpabilidade, aos antecedentes, à conduta social, à personalidade do agente, aos motivos, às circunstâncias e conseqüências do crime, bem como ao comportamento da vítima, estabelecerá, conforme seja necessário e suficiente para reprovação e prevenção do crime:

readings.description: Only final convictions that do not amount to reincidência count; there is no time limit on them; pending inquiries and prosecutions never count.
Art. 64, I's five-year purge applies to antecedentes by analogy: a conviction whose penalty ended more than five years before the new offence no longer counts.
Pending inquiries and prosecutions are part of the agent's antecedentes and may raise the pena-base.

question: How is the increase 'de um sexto a dois terços' for crime continuado chosen: by the judge within the range, or by the number of offences?
quote: aplica-se-lhe a pena de um só dos crimes, se idênticas, ou a mais grave, se diversas, aumentada, em qualquer caso, de um sexto a dois terços.

readings.description: The Code gives a range; the fraction within it is the judge's, to be reasoned.
The fraction follows the number of offences: 1/6 for two, 1/5 for three, 1/4 for four, 1/3 for five, 1/2 for six, 2/3 for seven or more.

rationale_hint: The brief keeps discretion with the judge, and the Code's range is the legal bound either way; but the STJ's consolidated scale is how the range is applied in practice. An Interpretation field with the scale as TYPICALLY and the bare range as the alternative keeps both executable and cites the súmula at the default.

question: In crime continuado, is prescription measured on the penalty including the art. 71 increase, or without it?
quote: Art. 119 - No caso de concurso de crimes, a extinção da punibilidade incidirá sobre a pena de cada um, isoladamente.

readings.description: Without it: prescription is governed by the penalty imposed for the crime, not counting the continuation increase.
With it: art. 71 treats the continued crimes as one, so the single penalty, increased, is the one art. 110 measures; art. 119 speaks of concurso and does not reach the fiction.

question: When the law changes while a crime continuado or permanente is still under way, which law governs it?
quote: Art. 4º - Considera-se praticado o crime no momento da ação ou omissão, ainda que outro seja o momento do resultado.

readings.description: The law in force when the continuation or permanence ceases governs the whole, even if more severe, provided it came into force before the cessation.
Art. 2's lex mitior and art. 4's 'momento da ação' fix the law at the first act, so a later, more severe law does not reach the conduct.

question: When do police preparation or surveillance make consummation 'impossível' within art. 17, whose words name only the means and the object?
quote: Art. 17 - Não se pune a tentativa quando, por ineficácia absoluta do meio ou por absoluta impropriedade do objeto, é impossível consumar-se o crime.

readings.description: A flagrante prepared by the police so that consummation is impossible is no crime; mere surveillance (electronic monitoring, security staff) does not by itself make the crime impossible.
Art. 17 reaches only absolute inefficacy of the means or absolute impropriety of the object; police preparation is outside it.
Any surveillance that would inevitably stop the theft makes it impossible within art. 17.

rationale_hint: Whether preparation made consummation impossible is a finding about the facts; an input field ('a preparação policial tornou impossível a consumação') carries it, and the rule applies Súmula 145 to that fact.

question: Is art. 75's 40-year ceiling a limit on time served only, or the base on which livramento condicional and regime progression are computed?
quote: § 1º Quando o agente for condenado a penas privativas de liberdade cuja soma seja superior a 40 (quarenta) anos, devem elas ser unificadas para atender ao limite máximo deste artigo.

readings.description: The ceiling limits time served; fractions for benefits are computed on the total penalty imposed.
The unified penalty replaces the total for every purpose, including the fractions of art. 83.

question: May the judge set an initial regime more severe than art. 33, § 2º's criteria allow for the penalty applied, and on what grounds?
quote: § 3º - A determinação do regime inicial de cumprimento da pena far-se-á com observância dos critérios previstos no art. 59 deste Código.

readings.description: Only with an idoneous, concrete reason drawn from the art. 59 circumstances; the abstract gravity of the offence is never enough, and with the pena-base at the minimum a harsher regime on gravity alone is barred.
Art. 33, § 3º's reference to art. 59 lets the judge weigh the offence's gravity as such.

rationale_hint: The encoding can compute the regime § 2º allows and treat a harsher one as permitted only when an input records a concrete art. 59 ground; it cannot judge whether a reason is idoneous.

question: What initial regime may a reincidente sentenced to eight years or less receive, given that § 2º, b and c speak only of the 'não reincidente' and § 2º, a assigns the fechado only above eight years?
quote: b) o condenado não reincidente, cuja pena seja superior a 4 (quatro) anos e não exceda a 8 (oito), poderá, desde o princípio, cumpri-la em regime semi-aberto;

readings.description: At four years or less, semiaberto is admissible if the art. 59 circumstances are favourable. The súmula says nothing above four years; there the reincidente's exclusion from § 2º, b leaves the most severe regime the species allows (for detenção, art. 33 caput keeps the initial regime to semiaberto or aberto).
Every reincidente starts in fechado: § 2º grants the milder regimes only to the não reincidente.

question: Does the confession atenuante require that the judge used the confession to convict, and does a partial or qualified confession count?
quote: d) confessado espontaneamente, perante a autoridade, a autoria do crime;

readings.description: Any spontaneous confession of authorship attenuates, whether or not the judge relied on it; a partial or qualified confession (e.g. admitting possession for personal use, denying trafficking) attenuates in a smaller proportion than a full one.
The confession attenuates only if used to form the judge's conviction, and a qualified confession that denies the offence charged does not attenuate.

citations.cite: STJ, Súmula 545 and Súmula 630 in their wording before the 10/09/2025 revision

question: Is the duration of a security measure (internação or tratamento ambulatorial) bounded?
quote: § 1º - A internação, ou tratamento ambulatorial, será por tempo indeterminado, perdurando enquanto não for averiguada, mediante perícia médica, a cessação de periculosidade. O prazo mínimo deverá ser de 1 (um) a 3 (três) anos.

readings.description: As printed: no maximum; the measure lasts until a medical examination finds the dangerousness has ceased.
readings.foreclosure: Foreclosed in STJ practice by Súmula 527; no court has struck it in abstract review as far as this sweep reached.

readings.description: Bounded by the maximum penalty abstractly cominated for the act committed.
Bounded by art. 75's general ceiling on time served (the line associated with the STF, not retrieved in this sweep; stated here without an authority quote).
readings.foreclosure: Not retrieved: portal.stf.jus.br was unreachable. Recorded so the encoder knows the STF line may differ from the STJ's.

question: Does a falta grave restart the count of the fraction of the penalty that art. 83 requires for livramento condicional?
quote: b) não cometimento de falta grave nos últimos 12 (doze) meses; (Incluído pela Lei nº 13.964, de 2019)

readings.description: No: the fraction runs from the start of execution regardless; since 2019 a falta grave in the last twelve months is a separate bar under art. 83, III, b.
Yes: the fraction is counted afresh from the last falta grave.

question: If the período de prova ends while a prosecution for a crime committed during the livramento is pending, but the livramento was never suspended or revoked, is the penalty extinct?
quote: Art. 89 - O juiz não poderá declarar extinta a pena, enquanto não passar em julgado a sentença em processo a que responde o liberado, por crime cometido na vigência do livramento.

readings.description: Yes: absent suspension or revocation before the período de prova ends, punibilidade is extinct (art. 90); art. 89 operates only through a timely suspension.
No: art. 89 bars extinction whenever such a prosecution is pending, whether or not the livramento was suspended.

question: What does the extinção da punibilidade by indulto reach: every effect of the conviction, or only the claim to execute the penalty?
quote: II - pela anistia, graça ou indulto;

readings.description: Only the primary effect (the executória claim); secondary effects survive — the conviction still counts for reincidência, and the effects of arts. 91–92 stand.
Extinção da punibilidade by indulto extinguishes the conviction's effects generally, as anistia does.

question: Is the sentence granting perdão judicial a conviction with every effect but reincidência (art. 120 a contrario), or a declaratory decision with no condemnatory effect?
quote: Art. 120 - A sentença que conceder perdão judicial não será considerada para efeitos de reincidência.

readings.description: Declaratory of extinção da punibilidade; no condemnatory effect survives.
Condemnatory: art. 120 excludes only reincidência, so other effects (e.g. the duty to indemnify under art. 91, I) survive.

question: Does the pronúncia keep its interruptive effect when the jury later reclassifies the crime to one outside its competence?

readings.description: Yes: the pronúncia interrupts regardless of the later reclassification.
No: once the jury reclassifies, the pronúncia is treated as never having interrupted prescription.

question: Does art. 110 caput's one-third increase for the reincidente reach the prescription of the punitive claim (art. 109, and the retroactive or intercurrent prescription of art. 110, § 1º)?
quote: Art. 110 - A prescrição depois de transitar em julgado a sentença condenatória regula-se pela pena aplicada e verifica-se nos prazos fixados no artigo anterior, os quais se aumentam de um terço, se o condenado é reincidente.

readings.description: No: the increase applies only to the executória prescription after final conviction; reincidência does not affect the punitive claim.
Yes, at least for § 1º, which also measures by the penalty applied and sits in the same article.

question: Does an acórdão that confirms a first-instance conviction (keeping, lowering or raising the penalty) interrupt prescription under art. 117, IV?
quote: IV - pela publicação da sentença ou acórdão condenatórios recorríveis;

readings.description: Yes: a condemnatory acórdão always interrupts, including a confirmatory one, whatever it does to the penalty.
Only an acórdão that convicts for the first time (reversing an acquittal) or materially changes the penalty interrupts; a mere confirmation does not.
